title: Albert J. Weatherhead, Jr. Professor of Business Administration
bio: Overview In his research, Professor Beshears shows how managers can influence the behavior of customers and employees by changing the decision-making environment to call attention to a decision, to use psychological framing to shape assessments of options, or to help individuals follow through on their intended behaviors. One example of this research involved working with a company to encourage employees to make an active choice between home delivery of prescription drugs and in-person pickup of prescription drugs at the pharmacy. By calling attention to the choice between the two options, this approach increased the adoption rate of home delivery from 6% to 42%, reducing financial costs for both the employees and the company that employed them. Keywords: Behavioral Economics ; Consumer Finance ; Household Finance ; Health Care ; Organizational Economics ; Decision Making ; Economics ; Negotiation ; Behavioral Finance

Weatherhead, Jr. Professor of Business Administration Albert J. Weatherhead, Jr. Professor of Business Administration John Beshears is the Albert J. Weatherhead Jr. Professor of Business Administration in the Negotiation, Organizations & Markets Unit, teaching the second-year MBA course "Negotiation." He is also a research associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research. Before joining HBS, he was an assistant professor of finance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business.
